APPROVED ON NOVEMBER 18, 2026

# REGULAR MEETING OF THE SOUTH BURLINGTON SCHOOL BOARD

Wednesday, November 4, 2026
Executive Session at 5:00 pm
Regular Session at 6:00 pm
South Burlington School District Administrative Office
577 Dorset Street, South Burlington, VT

## REGULAR MEETING

### PRESENT

Seamus Abshere (Zoom), Jennifer Lawrence, Dan Boyer, Michelle Boyer, Thomas Chittenden, Emilee Hoffman

### ADMINISTRATION/STAFF

Dr. Joe Clark, Daisy Brayton, Nick Bocchino

### GUESTS

None

### Call Regular meeting to order

Vice Chair Jennifer Lawrence called the meeting to order at 5:00 p.m.

## EXECUTIVE SESSION

The Board convened in Executive Session at 5:01 p.m.

Jennifer Lawrence called for a motion to enter executive session at 5:01 p.m. to discuss employment of a public officer or employee, receive confidential attorney-client communication for the purpose of providing legal services to the Board, labor negotiations, and real estate as permitted under Vermont law and added that it would be significantly disadvantageous to the District not to do so in executive session.

Dan Boyer moved, and Thomas Chittenden seconded. All in favor; the motion passed.

Discussion of employment of a public officer or employee, receive confidential attorney-client communication for the purpose of providing legal services to the Board, labor negotiations, and real estate.

IN: 5:01 p.m.
OUT: 5:35 p.m.
No Action

Thomas Chittenden moved to adjourn the executive session at 5:35 p.m. Dan Boyer seconded. All in favor; the motion passed. The executive session was adjourned.

Following the executive session, the Board took a tour of the newly renovated SouthPoint space at 577 Dorset Street. The Board returned to the regular meeting at 6:03 p.m.

## REGULAR MEETING

### PRESENT

Seamus Abshere (Zoom), Jennifer Lawrence, Dan Boyer, Michelle Boyer, Thomas Chittenden, Emilee Hoffman, Elissa Galvez, Oliver Kunz

### ADMINISTRATION/STAFF

Dr. Joe Clark, Jean-Marie Clark, Nicole Carter, Daisy Brayton, Nick Bocchino, Matthew Currier, Suzanne Gruendling, Lissa McDonald, Kat Yun, Beth Adreon

### GUESTS

Alex McHenry

### Call to Order

Vice Chair Jennifer Lawrence called the regular meeting to order at 6:03 p.m. The Pledge of Allegiance was said.

## ANNOUNCEMENTS AND AMENDMENTS TO THE AGENDA

### Announcements

Jennifer Lawrence thanked Katie Cunningham for the tour of the new SouthPoint space.

Jennifer Lawrence acknowledged the recent election and noted the importance of the democratic process, civic participation, and the freedom to peacefully elect leaders, expressing appreciation for the democratic principles upon which the country was founded.

Jennifer Lawrence stated that she, Elissa Galvez, and Joe Clark attended the Vermont School Board's Association Annual Meeting, participating in professional development sessions and networking with school board members from across the state. The attendees expressed appreciation for the opportunity and found the experience valuable.

### Amendment to Agenda

Seamus Abshere noted that the agenda incorrectly listed Policy F4 and Policy D9 as discussion items, which was a clerical error. He suggested amending the agenda to make them action items in order to take action on them at tonight's meeting.

Jennifer Lawrence suggested adding the review of the Board's public comment guidelines and agenda template to assess potential revisions while ensuring consistent enforcement and preserving the public's right to participate. Seamus Abshere indicated that he was waiting for legal review, but that it could be discussed at tonight's meeting.

Emilee Hoffman moved to approve the agenda with the modifications mentioned. Michelle Boyer seconded the motion. All were in favor, and the motion passed.

## Comments and Questions

South Burlington resident Alex McHenry raised concerns regarding the District's handling of a previously initiated but unfinished personnel investigation, referencing the SBEA's 2025 public complaint. Drawing comparisons to institutional failures involving the Catholic Church, Alex McHenry emphasized the importance of accountability, consistent application of personnel procedures, and avoiding favoritism. He expressed concerns about staff trust, student perceptions of accountability, and potential insurance and legal liabilities, and urged the District to restart and complete the investigation.

There were no additional comments or questions.

## FOCUS ON STUDENT LEARNING

Oliver Kunz provided the Board with a school update highlighting a successful fall athletic season, including the boys golf team winning its second consecutive state championship and four other teams reaching the state semifinals. Students were encouraged to register for winter sports. The middle school held a Wolfpack poster competition involving 40 advisories, with posters displayed in the lobby. Chamberlain Elementary will host a family movie night on December 6 at 6:00 p.m. The District also noted the upcoming school closures for Diwali (November 10) and Thanksgiving break.

There were no questions.

## DISCUSSION ITEMS

### The Other Paper Article Calendar and Production Process

The Board discussed developing a monthly newspaper article for The Other Paper to provide the community with a more cohesive understanding of district priorities, board governance, superintendent implementation, accountability, resource management, and student outcomes. Four proposed themes were identified: board leadership, governance and accountability, district stewardship, and student success and impact. Articles would be brief and accessible, with QR codes linking to supporting information on the District website. A proposed topic schedule running from November through October 2027 was presented, with potential topics including strategic planning, policy governance, accountability, budgeting, staff recognition, and student success. The Board also discussed identifying two or three authors to develop the articles while ensuring compliance with open meeting requirements. Board members were invited to review the proposed topics and volunteer to participate in drafting future articles. Joe Clark will also share this with the leadership team for their input.

### Executive Limitations Revision

The Board discussed reviewing the District's Executive Limitations policies to ensure they remain current and appropriately aligned with the recently updated Ends Policies. Jennifer Lawrence noted that six of the twelve policies had not been updated in more than two years, while others had no recent revision dates or remained pending. Potential deletions, additions, and modifications were discussed, with an emphasis on making only necessary, limited revisions while maintaining the intent of the policy governance framework. The Board agreed to revisit the topic at a future meeting, allowing members time to review assigned policies in greater depth and bring forward recommendations. No delegation or assignments were made at this time, and Joe Clark was invited to provide input.

Joe Clark shared feedback on the Executive Limitations monitoring process, noting that the policies are lengthy and difficult to report against because they require demonstrating that prohibited actions have not occurred. The Board discussed opportunities to simplify the policies and make monitoring reports more meaningful and efficient, potentially seeking guidance from the VSBA. The Board agreed the matter was important, but not urgent, and added it to the parking lot for future discussion. Existing monitoring reports will continue in the meantime.

### Act 170 Merger Committee Update on Nov 2 Meeting

The Board received an update on the November 2nd Act 170 Merger Committee meeting, which is studying the potential consolidation of South Burlington, Burlington, and Winooski school districts, including possible combinations. The committee requested district data and a strength-based asset mapping identifying existing district strengths and challenges. Potential strengths discussed included strong academic opportunities, a broad range of student programs, dedicated educators, and community partnerships. Challenges included aging facilities, building maintenance costs, and capacity and resource constraints.

The Board agreed that Joe Clark would review and synthesize existing district data, including community feedback, staff input, and information gathered through the Ends Policy and strategic planning processes, to develop an initial draft of strengths and challenges for Board review. Joe Clark will provide the initial draft of district strengths and challenges to Seamus Abshere and Dan Boyer by late November. They will synthesize the information and present a proposed final version at the December 2 Board meeting for approval, with the goal of submitting it to the December 7 Merger Committee meeting. Jennifer Lawrence pointed out that the Merger Committee established a website which represents the three districts, and the link can be found on the School Board homepage. Seamus Abshere and Dan Boyer will continue representing the Board on the Merger Committee.

### Review of Public Comment Guidelines and Agenda Template

The Board discussed whether the existing public participation policy/procedure provides sufficient guidance for the Chair to manage public comment while protecting the public's right to participate. The discussion followed a recent meeting in which public comments became personally directed toward an individual staff member. Potential areas for clarification included strengthening the Chair's authority to interrupt or end inappropriate comments, clarifying expectations regarding comments about individual employees or students, and consistently enforcing the existing three-minute speaker time limit. The Board discussed whether these concerns could be addressed through consistent enforcement or whether amendments to the policy/procedure may be warranted.

The Board continued discussion of the public participation policy/procedure, including concerns regarding First Amendment protections for public comment criticizing public officials and employees, as well as the Board's responsibility to protect employee and student privacy. Members discussed the distinction between criticism of employees in their public roles and disclosure of private information, and the importance of maintaining appropriate time limits and consistent enforcement. The Board agreed to seek legal counsel review and recommendations regarding the proposed language, with the topic scheduled for further discussion at the November 18 meeting. The Chair also reiterated that public comment on action items would be limited to three minutes per speaker, with consistent enforcement of the time limit.

## ACTION ITEMS

### Policy F4 Investigation and Response to Harassment, Hazing, and Bullying of Students (Third Reading)

The Board considered the third reading of Policy F4, Investigation and Response to Harassment, Hazing, and Bullying of Students. Following review and discussion at the previous three meetings, and with the proposed revisions made available to the public, Emilee Hoffman made a motion and Elissa Galvez seconded the motion to adopt the policy. Hearing no further discussion, all were in favor and the motion passed by unanimous vote.

### Policy D9 Electronic Communications Between Employees and Students (Third Reading)

The Board considered the third reading of Policy D9 Electronic Communications Between Employees and Students. Following review and discussion at the previous three meetings, and with the proposed revisions made available to the public, Emilee Hoffman made a motion and Dan Boyer seconded the motion to adopt the policy. Hearing no further discussion, all were in favor and the motion passed by unanimous vote.

### Monitoring Report 2.7 Asset Protection

Jean-Marie Clark presented Monitoring Report 2.7 Asset Protection, as part of the ongoing policy governance process. Overall compliance was rated proficient, with areas for continued improvement identified in purchasing procedures, conflict-of-interest protections, and financial controls. The presentation highlighted improvements made to internal controls, including more consistent bank deposits, additional payroll oversight, and corrections to student activity account and nutritional services procurement procedures. Jean-Marie Clark noted that staff training and continued emphasis on obtaining purchase orders prior to purchases remain ongoing priorities, as recent audits identified areas needing further improvement. The Board was informed that additional audit feedback is being addressed and that the District will continue working to strengthen financial oversight and safeguard district resources.

A Board member asked how the District tracks deferred maintenance, prioritizes building repairs, and plans for long-term capital needs given the age of its facilities. Jean-Marie Clark reported that the District currently has limited deferred maintenance due to ongoing investments in building upkeep, including roof and boiler replacements, paving, flooring, and restroom renovations. She noted that future capital needs are being reviewed as part of the upcoming budget process and identified challenges associated with aging buildings, including outdated layouts and the presence of asbestos, lead, and PCBs, which increase the cost and complexity of renovations.

The Board also discussed the District's auditing practices in light of recent financial concerns involving another school district. Members discussed the value of periodically reviewing or changing audit firms or personnel to ensure independent oversight and fresh perspectives. Jean-Marie Clark described existing internal financial controls, including separation of purchasing and approval responsibilities, and emphasized the importance of following established procedures to prevent fraud and ensure accountability. Jennifer Lawrence recommended improving transparency through a comprehensive facilities condition assessment, a capital improvement plan, supporting documentation for compliance findings, and tracking maintenance costs over time.

Jennifer Lawrence offered the opportunity for public comment; there was none.
The Board was asked to consider a motion to monitor 2.7 Asset Protection, using the monitoring rubric included in the Board materials. Emilee Hoffman moved and Elissa Galvez seconded the motion. All were in favor and the motion passed.

Following discussion and review of compliance criteria and the District outcome overall compliance with policy goals, the Board unanimously found the compliance plan acceptable.

### Monitoring Report 2.8 Compensation and Benefits

Daisy Brayton presented Monitoring Report 2.8 Compensation and Benefits, and rated overall compliance as proficient. The report reviewed the District's practices related to employee compensation, benefits, employment agreements, salary structures, market competitiveness, and pension obligations. Daisy Brayton explained that employee compensation and benefits are incorporated into the annual budget, union compensation is administered through negotiated collective bargaining agreements, and non-union positions follow established classification and salary schedules. The District maintains appropriate checks and balances in preparing employment offers and contracts, ensures financial obligations align with available revenues, and has made no changes to existing pension benefits.

Daisy Brayton also identified areas for continued improvement, including reviewing and reducing the District's approximately 290 non-union support staff job titles and classifications, updating job descriptions, conducting regular market compensation analyses, and consistently auditing human resources processes and procedures. The District has strengthened its requirements for independent contractors, including background checks, liability insurance, and W9 documentation. Daisy Brayton emphasized the importance of maintaining competitive and consistent compensation practices, ensuring compliance with legal requirements, and aligning long-term staffing and financial commitments with the District's budget and strategic planning goals.

The Board discussed the Early Retirement Program and clarified that the incentives offered to eligible employees do not change existing pension benefits or payment structures. The program

encourages eligible employees to retire voluntarily and may provide salary savings through the hiring of replacement staff at lower salary levels. The Board also discussed the District's ongoing compensation and classification review, including the recently received statewide market benchmarking data. Daisy Brayton explained that the District is reviewing job descriptions, salary classifications, and market competitiveness, with the goal of completing the process by the end of the fiscal year. Particular attention was given to positions that are difficult to fill and may require salary adjustments to remain competitive.

The Board also discussed historical inconsistencies in requirements for independent contractors, particularly the collection of liability insurance documentation. Daisy Brayton reported that requirements for background checks, liability insurance, and W9s are now being consistently enforced. Board members emphasized the importance of establishing clear timelines for improvement initiatives and providing measurable progress updates in future monitoring reports. Members also recommended using graphs and historical data to demonstrate trends in salary competitiveness and benchmarking over time, making compliance findings more transparent and understandable to both the Board and the public. Daisy Brayton agreed with the recommendations and noted the value of incorporating measurable data and visual representations into future reports.

The Board was asked to consider a motion to monitor 2.8 Compensation and Benefits, using the monitoring rubric included in the Board materials. Emilee Hoffman moved and Dan Boyer seconded the motion. All were in favor and the motion passed.

Following discussion and review of compliance criteria and the District outcome overall compliance with policy goals, the Board unanimously found the compliance plan acceptable.

### SUPERINTENDENT'S REPORT

Joe Clark gave the Board an update on the Chittenden Central Cooperative Educational Service Area (CESA), which voted unanimously to cancel its November and December meetings and resume regular meetings on January 25, 2027. The decision was made due to uncertainty surrounding Vermont's education transformation efforts, including potential district consolidation, future governance structures, funding, and the responsibilities of regional organizations. Members agreed that regional collaboration remains important but felt additional guidance from the state is needed before making significant organizational or financial commitments. The CESA may still call a special meeting if necessary before January.

In response to questions, it was noted that no funding is currently flowing to the CESA. Although $50,000 was designated for CEO recruitment and $15,000 for startup costs, accessing those funds requires an Employer Identification Number (EIN) and an established fiscal agent, neither of which has been finalized. The Board also heard that the CESA chairs had received responses and clarification from the Agency of Education regarding questions about the implementation process. Members will continue monitoring developments and exploring opportunities for regional collaboration while awaiting further state guidance.

Joe Clark provided an update on the FY28 budget development process, noting that work has begun in collaboration with district and school leaders to review enrollment, staffing, programs, class sizes, expenditures, and student needs. The goal is to identify opportunities for investment, resource reallocation, efficiencies, and potential reductions while ensuring alignment with district priorities. The initial budget meeting was held October 19, with additional meetings planned in November. No staffing or program decisions have been made, with the exception of posting an American Sign Language teacher position for the upcoming school year to support development of the program.

Joe Clark also outlined a new three-phase community engagement process, called the Budget Blitz, designed to provide multiple opportunities for public input through in-person and virtual meetings, prerecorded presentations, and online surveys. The first round is scheduled for November 16-20, followed by additional sessions in January and February to review the proposed budget and provide information ahead of Town Meeting Day on March 2, 2027. A dedicated FY28 budget webpage has been established to provide timelines, updates, presentations, and participation information. The preliminary budget is expected to be presented to the Board on December 2, with a target date of January 13 for Board approval. Board members discussed expanding outreach through city communication channels and website subscriptions to ensure broad community awareness. Joe Clark also noted an estimated 2.5% health insurance increase for the coming fiscal year and discussed potential efficiencies through centralized purchasing and supply management.

### CONSENT AGENDA

Jennifer Lawrence presented the Consent Agenda for Board consideration. Items approved included:

- Board meeting minutes of October 21, 2026
- Resignation(s)/Retirement(s)
  - Deborah Baker-Moody, 1.0 FTE Project SEARCH Regional Program for District

Jennifer Lawrence asked if there were any objections to the Consent Agenda. Hearing none, Thomas Chittenden moved to accept and Michelle Boyer seconded the motion. All were in favor; consent agenda was passed and items were approved.

### AGENDA FOR NEXT MEETING

The following items were added to the November 18, 2026, regular meeting agenda:

Focus on Student Learning:
- School Presentation by Gertrude Chamberlin School
- Student Representative Report

Discussion Items:
- Monthly Financial Review
- District Report Card (Nicole Carter)
- Public Comment/Participation Policy
- The Other Paper

Action Items:
- Monitoring Report 1.1 Rigorous Academic Achievement (Nicole Carter)
- Monitoring Report 1.2 Real Life Skills (Nicole Carter)
- Monitoring Report 2.11 Equity (Kat Yun)

### ADJOURNMENT

There being no further business, Jennifer Lawrence called for a motion to adjourn. Thomas Chittenden moved and Michelle Boyer seconded. Motion carried unanimously and the meeting adjourned at 8:53 p.m.
